payload.question_text: A radiology team must choose a Foundry option for reviewing X-ray images alongside clinicians' written questions. Which choices best fit this decision? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: GPT-4.1 can process images and text together. It meets the required input types.
GPT-4.1-mini is also a general-purpose multimodal model. It supports the required combined input processing.
Image generation creates or edits images. The decision requires understanding X-rays and answering written questions.
options.better_fit: Use this when the goal is to create or edit visual content.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could create an image rather than receive an interpretation.
feedback.instructional: Choose a multimodal model when image and text understanding are both required.

options.rationale: Foundry includes partner models with text and image understanding. Such a model can fit the required capability.

options.error_type: Confuses image analysis with video generation
options.rationale: Video generation creates video content. The decision requires interpreting X-rays and answering written questions.
options.better_fit: Use this when the goal is to create original video content.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could create a video rather than receive an interpretation of the X-rays.
feedback.instructional: Choose a multimodal model when image and text understanding are required; choose a video generation model only when creating video content.

payload.explanation: Correct. These choices support the required text-and-image understanding.

The image-generation option is a credible but non-defensible distractor because the source distinguishes image understanding from image creation. However, the multi-select item provides only one distractor, limiting diagnostic contrast.

The existing distractor diagnoses confusing visual interpretation with image generation, a source-grounded misconception. Because only one misconception is represented, the item has limited coverage of realistic errors such as confusing video generation with image analysis.

The ordered mechanics progress from recalling a model-family member, to understanding a causal statement, to analyzing a practical Foundry selection. The first item is somewhat peripheral to the stated SLO but still supports model identification.

The radiology-team decision to review X-rays alongside written questions is a credible application of the source's medical-imaging and multimodal-model examples.

Feedback identifies the relevant concepts, especially the distinction between image understanding and generation, but the first two items use brief generic explanations and provide limited learner next-step guidance.
The sequence combines foundational recall with understanding and application-level selection, appropriate for a Level 3 session, though the opening recall item is relatively easy.
The artifact consistently uses the source's terms GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, multimodal model, image generation model, and text-and-image understanding.
The exact sequence is factually sound, varied, and increasingly applied. Its main weakness is limited misconception coverage in the final multi-select item and comparatively terse feedback.
